title: Single-cell dissociation of the model cnidarian sea anemone Exaiptasia diaphana
protocol: Select one adult Aiptasia approximately 0.5–1.5 cm in total diameter, including tentacles.
Fill three wells of a 6-well plate with CMF-ASW+EGTA.
Move the selected animal to the first well of the prepared 6-well plate using a transfer pipette.
Gently pipette the animal in and out of the pipette to wash.
Repeat the washing process two additional times by transferring the anemone to the second and third wells of the 6-well plate.
Take as little of the washing media as possible for each transfer when moving the animal between wells.
Use suction from a clean transfer pipette to remove the Aiptasia anemone from the final washing well, taking minimal washing media.
Place the animal on an empty, inverted petri dish for dissection.
Remove the tentacles from the animal and chop them into fine pieces.
Orient the tentacles in one direction.
Cut the animal where the tentacles meet the body.
Remove and discard the body.
Chop the tentacles vertically and horizontally with a razor blade.
Use a p200 pipette to orient the animal under a dissection microscope.
Dissect all tentacles from the body using a razor blade.
Drag the body away from the tentacles and discard.
Finely chop the tentacles horizontally and vertically with a razor blade.
Resuspend the chopped tentacle pieces in 200 μL of CMF-ASW+EGTA.
Transfer the resuspended tentacle pieces to a pre-weighed 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the chopped tentacle pieces at 70 × g for 5 minutes.
Gently remove and discard the supernatant from the animal pellet.
Weigh the tube containing the pelleted tentacles after removing supernatant.
Subtract the mass of the empty tube from the total mass to determine the tentacle mass in milligrams.
Prepare fresh 0.5% pronase solution by mixing 200 μL CMF-ASW+EGTA with 200 μL 1% pronase CMF-ASW+EGTA.
Add 400 μL of 0.5% pronase solution to the tissue pellet containing tentacles.
Mix the tentacle pieces in the pronase solution slowly and gently by pipetting up and down approximately eight times until well mixed.
Incubate the tentacle pieces on an orbital shaker at 25°C with gentle agitation for approximately 0.7 min per milligram of tentacle mass.
Continue incubation until no visible tissue chunks remain in the solution.
Suspend chopped tentacles in pronase and Hoechst 33342 solution for staining.
Incubate the suspension on an orbital shaker at 25°C until no visible tissue chunks remain.
Centrifuge dissociated cells at 70 × g for 5 min after enzymatic digestion.
Gently remove and discard the supernatant to ensure clarity.
Proceed to centrifugation and resuspension for microscopy.
Suspend dissociated cells in 200 μL of staining solution.
Flick the tube gently to mix the cells with the staining solution.
Incubate the cells for 30 min in the dark at 25°C.
Centrifuge the cells at 70 × g for 5 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant (staining solution).
Resuspend the cells in 8–24 μL of CMF-ASW+EGTA.
Mount the cell suspension on a microscope slide using a pipette to take 8–10 μL.
Lower a 22 mm × 22 mm coverslip over the droplet until flat, avoiding bubbles.
Seal the coverslip to the slide using clear nail polish or an alternative sealer.
Allow the sealant to dry completely before viewing the slide on a fluorescence microscope.
